title: Best Accounting Software for Multi-Currency: 9 Tools Compared
summary: Compare 9 tools for multi-currency operations: exchange rates, FX gains and losses, consolidation, payments and reconciliation.
body_markdown:
The best accounting software for multi-currency depends on how far your currency work goes. If you mostly invoice and pay in a few foreign currencies, a **small business ledger** with automatic exchange rates covers it; if you translate and consolidate several entities into one reporting currency, you need an **ERP or financial management system** built for multi-entity consolidation.


This guide compares nine tools: Simetrik, Xero, QuickBooks Online, Zoho Books, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Workday, Tipalti and PayPal. Simetrik isn’t accounting software. It’s an **AI-native financial control platform** that reconciles the cross-currency transaction data your multi-currency accounting software depends on, so FX differences in fees, refunds and settlements show up before they reach the books.


If your company sells in several currencies, you probably know how this goes at month-end.


A processor settles a payout short because it applied its own exchange rate. A refund gets converted at a different rate than the original sale. A euro bank account doesn’t tie to the ledger after revaluation. Each one becomes an **unexplained FX variance** that someone has to trace back by hand.


### Key takeaways


- **Three jobs:** multi-currency accounting software does three things: record transactions in foreign currencies, revalue open balances as rates move, and translate entities into one reporting currency. Small business ledgers focus on the first two; consolidation is where ERPs and financial management systems come in.
- **Fit by size:** Xero, QuickBooks Online and Zoho Books fit small teams; NetSuite, Sage Intacct and Workday fit multi-entity groups; Tipalti and PayPal move money across currencies.
- **Reconciliation layer:** Simetrik works alongside the best accounting software for multi-currency: it reconciles transaction data from processors and banks, including FX differences on settlements, before that data is posted.
- **Plan and edition matter.** Several vendors limit multi-currency features to specific tiers, so check the plan before you compare features.


## Why Multi-Currency Accounting Software Matters


Multi-currency accounting software records, converts and reports foreign currency transactions so your books stay accurate in one base currency. Without it, someone looks up exchange rates, handles currency conversion on each invoice and bill, and works out the gain or loss when payment arrives at a different rate.


The work splits into **three jobs** : recording deals in the currency they happened in, revaluing open balances at period end, and translating each entity’s results into the group’s reporting currency for consolidated financial statements.


**Currency fluctuations** are why all three matter. Rates move between the transaction date and the payment date, and the difference has to land in the[general ledger](https://simetrik.com/glossary/general-ledger/) as a **realized or unrealized gain or loss** .


There’s a **fourth job** most comparisons skip: confirming that the amounts and rates your processors and banks actually applied match what your books expect. That’s **reconciliation work** , and it happens at the transaction level, before revaluation or consolidation runs.


## Key Multi-Currency Features to Evaluate


The features below separate tools that handle a second currency from tools that handle a multi-currency business.


- **Live exchange rates** : rates pulled automatically from a named source, with the option to override a rate on a single transaction when you’ve agreed a fixed rate.
- **Multi-currency invoicing** : billing customers and receiving bills in their own currency, with each contact assigned a default currency.
- **Foreign currency accounts** : bank accounts and balances held in other currencies without forcing an immediate conversion.
- **Realized and unrealized gains and losses** : calculated automatically on payment and at period-end revaluation.
- **Functional currency by entity** : each subsidiary keeps its own ledger currency, separate from the group’s reporting currency.
- **Multi-entity consolidation** : currency translation rules, intercompany eliminations and consolidated reporting across entities.
- **Financial reporting in more than one currency** : reports in local and reporting currencies, with revenue recognition and cash flow views that reflect rate movements.
- **Audit trails** : a record of which rate was applied to each transaction and who changed it.
- **Standards and local rules** : translation that supports GAAP (ASC 830) or IFRS (IAS 21) reporting, plus local tax handling such as GST or VAT where you operate.
- **Transaction-level verification** : a way to check processor and bank data, including fees and FX applied on settlements, against your own records.


The last item sits in a different layer from the rest of the list. It matters most when cash comes in through several payment providers in several currencies.

Each tool was reviewed on the **same criteria** : what it is and where it sits in the finance stack, how it sources and applies exchange rates, whether it handles multi-entity consolidation, which plans include multi-currency, and how it uses AI.

## Which Tool Fits Which Team


Match the tool to the job you need done, then check whether a second tool covers the layer next to it.


If your main need is… Start with Why


Verifying FX, fees and settlements across processors and banks Simetrik Transaction-level reconciliation before data reaches the ledger


Invoicing and paying in a few foreign currencies Xero, QuickBooks Online or Zoho Books Automatic rates and per-contact currencies in a small business ledger


Consolidating many subsidiaries across currencies NetSuite or Sage Intacct Native multi-entity consolidation and currency translation


Running finance and workforce data on one platform Workday Financial management on a shared foundation with HR data


Paying suppliers and subsidiaries worldwide Tipalti Global payables with FX built into the payment workflow


Accepting international payments online PayPal Collects in other currencies and converts or holds balances


**Most multi-currency businesses end up with more than one of these.** A marketplace, for example, might run NetSuite as its ledger, pay sellers through a payouts provider and use Simetrik to reconcile what its processors and banks actually settled.


## Best Accounting Software for Multi-Currency, Reviewed


Each review uses the same fields so you can compare tools line for line.


### 1. Simetrik


**What it is:** Simetrik is an AI-native financial control platform that reconciles transaction and operational data, from ingestion to accounting. It isn’t accounting software and doesn’t replace your ledger; it works on the records that feed it. According to Simetrik, the platform processes 2.5 billion records a day across 50+ countries.


**Best for:** Simetrik is the best fit when your multi-currency books depend on transaction data from many processors, banks and internal systems, and you need automation and traceability over the FX differences hidden in fees, refunds and settlements.


Payment service providers,[marketplaces](https://simetrik.com/industries/marketplaces/) and merchants selling across countries are examples, but the fit comes from the need for automation and traceability, not only from high volume.


**Where it sits in the stack:** The reconciliation and financial control layer, before and as data reaches the ledger. Simetrik complements the accounting software, ERPs and payment platforms in this list.


**Key capabilities:**


- **Multi-currency transaction control:** According to Simetrik’s page for payment service providers, fees are validated per payment method, country and currency, and FX rates are confirmed across multi-currency settlements. Its[reconciliation engine](https://simetrik.com/reconciliation-software/) matches records one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many, with tolerances and chained reconciliations, and its published template categories include FX and crypto.
- **AI that builds and investigates:** Using the data already in Simetrik, AI can investigate and manage differences on its own at the autonomy level your team sets, and it creates and analyzes datasets and trends in plain language, so you can see FX and fee patterns across processors or banks without building reports by hand.
- **Simetrik Agent and MCP:**[Simetrik Agent](https://simetrik.com/reconciliation-software/simetrik-agent/) builds and adjusts reconciliations from plain-language requests, with three autonomy levels (Automatic, Confirmation, which Simetrik recommends, and Planning), and teams can connect agents such as Claude or Copilot through[MCP](https://simetrik.com/reconciliation-software/mcp/) .
- **Named AI capabilities:** These include Smart Parser for non-standard processor and bank files, Smart Date Formats (Simetrik cites 500+ formats) and Anomaly Detection. Results come from a **deterministic core** : the same inputs and rules produce the same result, which keeps every AI action traceable for an auditor.
- **Exception handling:** Chargebacks, refunds, short settlements and unexpected fees are separated as differences and identified in dashboards where your team acts on them, individually or in bulk, with alerts by email, Slack or SMS.
- **Accounting handoff:** Simetrik generates journal entries from reconciliation results through configuration, connects to ERPs such as SAP S/4HANA, Oracle or NetSuite, and adapts the posting to how each system requires entries to be recorded.


**How AI is used:** AI investigates and manages differences, analyzes FX and fee trends, and builds controls through Simetrik Agent or MCP; the deterministic engine produces the results.


**Worth knowing:** Simetrik doesn’t market consolidation. Currency translation, revaluation and consolidation stay with your accounting software or ERP, and Simetrik supplies them with reconciled transaction data.


A small business with one bank account and one processor may not need a dedicated reconciliation platform; the need grows with the number of sources and with how much of the close auditors need to trace back to the original records.


### 2. Xero


**What it is:** Xero is cloud accounting software for small businesses, with multi-currency accounting built into the same ledger.


**Best for:** Small businesses that invoice international customers and pay overseas suppliers in their own currencies.


**Where it sits in the stack:** Small business accounting (general ledger and bookkeeping).


**Key capabilities:**


- Supports over 160 currencies for invoices, bills, bank accounts and expense claims, converted to your base currency automatically.
- Updates exchange rates hourly and lets you override the rate on an individual invoice, bill or payment.
- Assigns a default currency to each contact, so quotes, invoices and purchase orders use it.
- Offers a currency revaluation feature to update the home-currency value of open foreign balances at month-end.
- Reports in local or foreign currencies, including foreign currency exposure and how rate movements affect cash flow and profits.


**How AI is used:** JAX, Xero’s AI companion, answers questions about your business’s financials and helps with admin tasks such as creating invoices and quotes.


**Worth knowing:** In the US, Xero includes multi-currency on its Established plan. Xero also suggests connecting a payment processor that supports multiple currencies, such as Stripe or PayPal, to accept payment on foreign invoices.


### 3. QuickBooks Online


**What it is:** QuickBooks Online is Intuit’s cloud accounting software for small businesses. Its Multicurrency feature records transactions in foreign currencies and converts them to your home currency.


**Best for:** Small businesses already running bookkeeping in QuickBooks that need to record foreign invoices, bills and bank accounts.


**Key capabilities:**


- Multicurrency is available in QuickBooks Online Essentials, Plus and Advanced.
- Assigns one currency to each customer, vendor and account in the chart of accounts, such as a foreign bank or credit card account.
- Updates exchange rates automatically every four hours, or lets you enter your own rates.
- Converts foreign transactions to your home currency, and supports deposits and transfers between accounts in different currencies.


**How AI is used:** Intuit AI includes agents that automate accounting workflows to keep books up to date; Intuit says its AI suggests fixes for anomalies while you decide the next step.


**Worth knowing:** Intuit notes that turning on Multicurrency is permanent and fixes your home currency, so it’s worth deciding on your setup before you enable it.


### 4. Zoho Books


**What it is:** Zoho Books is cloud accounting software from Zoho, with multi-currency transactions, multilingual invoicing and base currency adjustments.


**Best for:** Small businesses that want exchange rates updated automatically and customers and vendors handled in their own currencies.


**Key capabilities:**


- Sets your base currency from your business location (USD for a US organization) and lets you add currencies and assign them to customers or vendors.
- Updates exchange rates automatically through Exchange Rate Feeds from Open Exchange Rates, enabled by default, with an option to enter rates manually.
- Uses base currency adjustments to record the gain or loss caused by fluctuating exchange rates.


**How AI is used:** Zoho Books uses Zia, a conversational assistant that answers finance questions in plain English, plus machine-learning anomaly detection on reports and agentic AI that connects to other tools through MCP.


**Worth knowing:** Zoho notes that invoicing in multiple currencies is available only in certain Zoho Books plans.


### 5. NetSuite


**What it is:** NetSuite is a cloud ERP from Oracle. NetSuite OneWorld manages multiple subsidiaries, business units and legal entities in a single system.


**Best for:** Companies managing several subsidiaries across countries that want accounting, tax and consolidation in one ERP.


**Where it sits in the stack:** ERP and general ledger, with multi-entity consolidation.


**Key capabilities:**


- Supports more than 190 currencies and 27 languages.
- Consolidates financial results and produces consolidated financial statements across subsidiaries, restating currencies for reporting.
- Includes country-specific configurations for local accounting, tax and business standards.


**How AI is used:** NetSuite embeds AI across the suite, with agents that assist and advise by simplifying tasks, suggesting actions and surfacing business insights.


**Worth knowing:** OneWorld is NetSuite’s offering for multi-subsidiary operations, so it fits best once a company runs several legal entities.


If NetSuite is your ledger, Simetrik can sit in front of it: it reconciles processor and bank data first, then posts journal entries to NetSuite, adapting the posting to how NetSuite requires entries to be recorded.


### 6. Sage Intacct


**What it is:** Sage Intacct is a cloud accounting system that manages multiple entities in one system, with multi-currency consolidation among its capabilities.


**Best for:** Mid-sized teams consolidating several entities across currencies; Sage says Intacct is trusted by 30,000+ scaling and mid-sized teams.


**Where it sits in the stack:** Core accounting system with consolidation.


**Key capabilities:**


- Handles multi-entity, multi-currency and multi-level consolidations, with eliminations, currency translation rules and ownership structures by period.
- Automates cumulative translation adjustments for ASC 830 (FAS 52) multi-currency consolidation.
- Applies OANDA exchange rates automatically and generates reports in headquarters, subsidiary or parent currencies.
- Lets you drill into consolidation journals for audit traceability.


**How AI is used:** Sage Intacct includes a Close agent that tracks close tasks, a Financial Assurance agent that flags unusual journal entries against historical patterns, and an AP Automation agent for bill entry and PO matching.


**Worth knowing:** Sage presents multi-currency consolidation as one of Sage Intacct’s extended capabilities, so confirm it’s part of the configuration you’re quoted.


### 7. Workday


**What it is:** Workday Financial Management is a financial management system that runs on the same platform as Workday’s workforce data.


**Best for:** Global organizations that want finance, operational and workforce data in one system.


**Where it sits in the stack:** Financial management system (general ledger and accounting) for multi-entity organizations.


**Key capabilities:**


- Gives each company its own ledger currency and records transactions in other currencies, converting them automatically.
- Books realized gains and losses automatically when an invoice and its payment settle in different currencies.
- Supports multiple charts of accounts and books, with 56 prebuilt country-specific configurations and 15 languages.


**How AI is used:** Workday’s AI, Sana, automates work across finance and other functions, with finance agents that surface exceptions and suggest next actions.


**Worth knowing:** Workday’s documentation notes that teams maintain currency conversion rates between each company currency and the currencies they transact in.


### 8. Tipalti


**What it is:** Tipalti is an AP automation and global payments platform. It handles payables and cross-border payouts, while your accounting system keeps the books.


**Best for:** Finance teams paying international vendors, contractors and subsidiaries in many currencies.


**Where it sits in the stack:** AP automation and global payments, synced to the ERP.


**Key capabilities:**


- Pays suppliers and payees across 200+ countries and territories in 120 currencies, with 50+ payment methods.
- Holds and converts funds in 25 currencies, with live FX rates and conversion status.
- Manages AP across subsidiaries, entities and currencies from one system.
- Integrates with ERP and accounting systems such as NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks Online, Xero, Microsoft Dynamics and SAP Business One.


**How AI is used:** Tipalti AI includes an assistant and agents for invoice capture, matching bills to purchase orders, building reports and suggesting approvers.


**Worth knowing:** Tipalti focuses on payables and payouts, and syncs that activity with the ERP or accounting system that keeps your general ledger.


### 9. PayPal


**What it is:** PayPal is a payment platform. A PayPal Business account accepts payments from international buyers and can hold balances in foreign currencies.


**Best for:** Businesses selling online to customers in other countries who want to collect in the buyer’s currency.


**Where it sits in the stack:** Payment processing.


**Key capabilities:**


- Converts payments made in other currencies to USD automatically.
- Alternatively, holds balances in up to 21 currencies other than USD so you choose when to convert.
- Supports cards, digital wallets and local payment methods for international buyers.


**How AI is used:** PayPal’s Agent Ready lets businesses accept payments inside AI shopping experiences, as part of its agentic commerce services.


**Worth knowing:** PayPal says cross-border fees and currency conversion costs apply on top of the standard transaction fee, so compare total cost per transaction. Payments collected through PayPal still need to be recorded in your accounting software.


## Other Platforms You’ll See in Search Results


Two more Sage products appear often in multi-currency searches:


- **Sage 50:** Sage’s small business accounting software, formerly Peachtree. Sage’s help documentation for the Canadian edition covers turning on foreign currency transactions, adding currencies and updating exchange rates.
- **Sage Accounting:** On Sage’s Canadian site, multi-currency is listed as a Sage Accounting Plus feature, with live exchange rates and gain and loss tracking.


## How AI Is Changing Multi-Currency Accounting


AI in multi-currency accounting mostly shows up as assistants that answer questions and agents that take on routine entries. Xero’s JAX and Zoho Books’ Zia answer finance questions in plain language, QuickBooks Online and Sage Intacct use agents for bookkeeping, AP and anomaly flags, and Tipalti applies AI to invoice capture and PO matching.


**Simetrik** applies AI to the transaction data underneath, managing differences between processor, bank and internal records and analyzing FX and fee trends in plain language.


The useful question isn’t whether a tool has AI. It’s **what data the AI works on** and whether you can **show an auditor how each result was produced** . Sage Intacct’s agents work on journal entries and AP, Tipalti’s on invoices and approvals, and[Simetrik’s AI](https://simetrik.com/reconciliation-software/simetrik-ai/) on transaction and operational data, with results produced by a deterministic engine.


## How to Choose Accounting Software for Multi-Currency Operations


Start with two numbers: **how many currencies** you transact in today, and **how many legal entities** need to roll up into one set of books.


One entity with a handful of currencies points to a small business ledger; several entities with different functional currencies point to ERP systems or financial management platforms with native[financial consolidation](https://simetrik.com/glossary/financial-consolidation/) . Every tool in this list offers multi-currency support in some form, so the real comparison is how much currency management each one takes off your team.


**Then work through these questions with each vendor:**


1. Which plan includes multi-currency, and does turning it on change anything permanently, such as your home currency?
2. Where do exchange rates come from, how often do they update, and can you override a rate on one transaction?
3. Are realized and unrealized gains and losses calculated automatically, including period-end revaluation?
4. How do bank feeds and bank reconciliation work for foreign currency accounts?
5. Can accounts payable, purchase orders and expense tracking run in the supplier’s currency, and does it connect to your CRM?
6. If you consolidate, does it handle currency translation,[intercompany eliminations](https://simetrik.com/glossary/intercompany-eliminations/) and consolidated reporting natively, and what does scalability look like as you add countries?
7. Who checks the amounts and rates your processors and banks applied against your own records, and where does that check happen?


That last question is about the layer next to your accounting software.


If cash comes in through several processors in several currencies, a **reconciliation layer** catches FX and fee differences on each settlement before they turn into unexplained variances on the balance sheet. Simetrik’s guide on[how to choose a reconciliation software](https://simetrik.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-reconciliation-software/) covers those criteria in detail.


## Common Mistakes When Choosing Multi-Currency Accounting Software


- **Comparing features without checking the plan:** multi-currency often sits in a higher tier, and some settings are permanent once enabled.
- **Ignoring functional currency until the second entity:** setting each entity’s ledger currency correctly from the start avoids restating history later.
- **Treating settlement checks as a ledger job:** the ledger records the payout it receives; checking that payout against the rate and fees the processor should have applied is reconciliation work.
- **Letting a payments tool stand in for accounting:** payment platforms move and convert money, but the books still live in your accounting system.


## Multi-Currency Accounting Software FAQs


### Which accounting software supports multiple currencies?


**Most cloud accounting platforms support multiple currencies** , including Xero, QuickBooks Online, Zoho Books, NetSuite, Sage Intacct and Workday. The difference is depth: some cover invoicing and foreign bank accounts for one entity, while NetSuite, Sage Intacct and Workday also translate and consolidate several entities. Simetrik doesn’t keep the books; it reconciles the multi-currency transaction data those systems receive.


### Does QuickBooks Online support multiple currencies?


**Yes.** QuickBooks Online’s Multicurrency feature is available in the Essentials, Plus and Advanced plans. It assigns a currency to each customer, vendor and account, updates exchange rates every four hours and converts transactions to your home currency. Intuit notes that Multicurrency stays on once it’s enabled.


### What’s the difference between base currency and functional currency?


Base currency is the currency your books and reports are kept in, usually set by where your business is located. Functional currency is the currency of the main economic environment an entity operates in, as defined in ASC 830 and IAS 21.


In a multi-entity group, each subsidiary can have its own functional currency, and its results are translated into the group’s reporting currency for consolidated financial statements.


### What happens to currency fluctuations between the transaction date and payment date?


The difference is recorded as a foreign exchange gain or loss. When the invoice is paid, the difference becomes a realized gain or loss; while it’s still open at period end, revaluation records an unrealized one. Multi-currency accounting software calculates these entries using the rate on each date, instead of leaving them to a manual adjustment at close.


### Is multi-currency invoicing the same as multi-currency accounting?


No. Multi-currency invoicing means billing a customer in their own currency, which many invoicing and payment tools handle. Multi-currency accounting also covers foreign currency accounts, gains and losses, revaluation, functional currency by entity and consolidated financial statements.


### Does Simetrik replace my multi-currency accounting software?


No. Simetrik isn’t accounting software or an ERP; invoicing, revaluation and consolidation stay with your accounting system. Simetrik complements it: it reconciles transaction and operational data from processors, banks and internal systems, including fees and FX on settlements, and posts verified journal entries to ERPs such as NetSuite, adapting the posting to how each system requires it.


### How is Simetrik different from Xero, NetSuite or Tipalti?


Xero and NetSuite keep the books: they record foreign currency transactions, convert them and, in NetSuite’s case, consolidate subsidiaries. Tipalti pays vendors and subsidiaries across currencies.


Simetrik works on the transaction data around them, matching processor, bank and internal records and identifying fee and FX differences in dashboards before they reach the ledger. Rather than replacing these platforms, **Simetrik can complement any of them** .


### How does Simetrik use AI in multi-currency reconciliation?


Simetrik uses AI on the transaction and operational data it already holds. At the autonomy level a team sets, AI can investigate and manage differences on its own, and it creates and analyzes datasets and trends in plain language, such as FX and fee patterns by processor or country.


Simetrik Agent, or agents such as Claude and Copilot connected through MCP, also build and adjust reconciliations from plain-language requests (Automatic, Confirmation, which Simetrik recommends, or Planning). Results come from a deterministic core, so every AI action stays traceable for an auditor.


### Can AI automate multi-currency accounting?


Partly. Simetrik applies AI to transaction data before it reaches the ledger, managing differences and building reconciliations with Simetrik Agent or agents connected through MCP. In accounting software, Xero’s JAX and Zoho Books’ Zia answer finance questions in plain language, and Sage Intacct and QuickBooks Online use agents for bookkeeping, AP and anomaly flags. People still review the results and sign off the close.
